image_description: Two hockey pucks positioned side-by-side against a black background. The left puck features a white face with a red and orange graphic of a bear or mascot head and surrounding text. The right puck has a black face with a red circular center containing stylized text and a silver/grey curved logo element at the bottom. Both pucks show the characteristic cylindrical shape with visible side ridges.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Compact solid disk with diameter moderately exceeding its thickness, creating a stout cylindrical profile.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both objects clearly exhibit the standard hockey puck geometry: a short cylinder where diameter is significantly larger than height.
The objects appear solid and opaque with no signs of translucency or internal structure inconsistent with solid rubber.

While the base material is black, the faces are heavily decorated with white, red, and orange graphics. The 'matte black' description applies only to the unprinted side/edge, not the overall visual appearance of the faces shown.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both pucks feature prominent printed graphics. The left has a mascot/logo; the right has stylized text and a logo.

artifact_observations.location: Text on the left puck (white face) and right puck (red center)
artifact_observations.reasoning: The text elements on both pucks are illegible and distorted. On the left puck, the red text curving around the mascot is nonsensical glyph-like shapes rather than readable letters. On the right puck, the text in the red circle is similarly warped and unreadable. This is a common AI artifact where text structure is mimicked but character integrity fails.

artifact_observations.location: Edge of the left puck, specifically where the white face meets the black side
artifact_observations.reasoning: There is slight bleeding/blurring between the white printed face and the black rubber edge. The boundary is not perfectly sharp, suggesting a minor generation artifact in the transition between materials/colors.
